science.title: See the science
science.pLong: The p-value measures how compatible the observed data are with the assumption of no monotonic trend. A value below 0.05 is commonly considered statistically significant.
science.hr: Corrects the test for autocorrelation (when one year resembles the previous one). A robustness check of the same data, not an independent validation.
science.ic: 95% range of plausible slopes (Gilbert 1987); not corrected for autocorrelation, so it may be too narrow.
science.chartAlt: Yearly series of {what} at {place}, {period}. Dots are the published yearly values. The dashed line is Sen's slope. No uncertainty band is drawn. Evidence: {level}.
science.recordLabel: Published change over the whole record
science.mkRole: Asks whether a steady rise or fall in the yearly values would be unusual if there were no monotonic trend.
science.smkRole: Checks whether the change is consistent from month to month. It can make the result look too sure, so it is not used alone.
science.qRole: Accounts for the many tests we ran. Shown as information. It does not replace the verdict.
science.months: A typical year, month by month
science.cant1: Eleven places are not the average of the Congo Basin.
science.cant2: A trend is not a cause.
science.cant3: Yaoundé is outside the Congo hydrographic basin and inside the Congo Basin forest region (COMIFAC). The cell is about 55 by 70 km.
science.cant4: If the test is not significant, that is not proof that nothing happened. The label is: not enough evidence yet.
hr.confirms: Hamed-Rao agrees with the main test on this series.
hr.contradicts: Hamed-Rao does not agree with the main test on this series.
hr.none: Hamed-Rao is not available for this series.
acker.title: Five steps from the challenge author
acker.cite: Acker and colleagues (2009) describe the path as series, plot, trend, test, then interpretation. Each one is on this screen.
acker.series: Series — the yearly values are the published record.
acker.plot: Plot — the chart above shows those years.
acker.trend: Trend — Sen's slope is the dashed line, and the 95% range is written in numbers, not as a band.
acker.test: Test — Mann-Kendall, the seasonal test, Hamed-Rao, and the q value are in the table.
acker.meaning: Interpretation — the next step asks questions for a job. It does not give an order.
acker.open: Open the questions for a job
clue.pick: Choose a clue. The result opens at once. The plain name comes before the dataset name.
def.t2m: Air temperature about 2 metres above the ground, averaged over the year.
def.t2m_max: The hottest air temperature about 2 metres up, averaged over the year. This is the air, not the ground.
def.t2m_min: The coolest air temperature about 2 metres up, averaged over the year.
def.ts: Skin temperature of the ground in the model. Not the air temperature.
def.precip: Rain added up over the year.
def.rh2m: How much moisture the air holds, about 2 metres up. Counted in percentage points, not as rainfall.
def.solar: Sunlight reaching the surface, all skies included.
def.soil_root: How wet the soil is where roots grow, in the model. 0 is dry, 1 is saturated.
sourceType.merra2: Reanalysis: a weather model that also uses observations. Not a thermometer in the street.
sourceType.ceres: Satellite product for sunlight, served on the NASA POWER grid.
sourceType.modis_lst: Satellite land surface temperature. Pending — not used in the numbers.
sourceType.modis_ndvi: Satellite vegetation index. Pending — not used in the numbers.
sourceType.gpm_imerg: Satellite rainfall. Pending — not used in the numbers.
sourceType.hydrosheds: Outline of the river basin. A reference map, not a climate series.
method.title: Method, limits, and what comes next
method.intro: Every number in the app is read from the published file. Nothing is recalculated in the browser.
method.fromFile: As recorded in the results file
method.excluded: A downloaded variable that was not analysed
method.limit1: Eleven places are not a basin-wide average.
method.limit2: Yaoundé is about 63 km outside the Congo hydrographic basin, and inside the Congo Basin forest region (COMIFAC).
method.limit3: A trend does not show its cause.
method.limit4: The 95% range is not corrected for autocorrelation, so it may be too narrow.
method.limit5: The seasonal test assumes months are independent, so its p-value can be too small.
method.limit6: 198 tests were run. The results are exploratory. The q value is information.
method.limit7: Each point is a model cell of about 55 by 70 km, not a weather station and not a neighbourhood.
method.limit8: MODIS, GPM, forest loss, and a worldwide search are not in this version. They are marked pending or coming soon.
method.repro: Reproduced: the statistics were produced with pymannkendall 1.4.3. This website only displays them.
method.compare: Compare: other datasets (MODIS, GPM, KNMI) are not in this version. The 11 places can already be compared with each other.
method.validate: An independent check against another dataset has not been done. Only the reproduction step is done.
method.nextBody: Neighbourhood maps, satellite rain, vegetation, and places outside the Congo Basin are the next steps. They are visible in the interface and carry no numbers yet.
method.aiBody: The statistics were not written by a chat assistant. They come from the team's Python script (pymannkendall 1.4.3) and the published results file. A coding agent in Cursor drafted the screens and the plain-language sentences from the team's roadmap and from that file. It did not recompute a p-value, a slope, or an evidence level. The team still reads the wording before a public demo. Pending datasets are not filled with stand-in numbers.
cite.mann: Mann, H. B. (1945). Nonparametric tests against trend. Econometrica, 13(3), 245–259. DOI 10.2307/1907187.
cite.kendall: Kendall, M. G. (1975). Rank Correlation Methods, 4th ed. Charles Griffin. Book, no DOI.
cite.hirsch: Hirsch, R. M., Slack, J. R. & Smith, R. A. (1982). Techniques of trend analysis for monthly water quality data. Water Resources Research, 18(1), 107–121. DOI 10.1029/WR018i001p00107.
cite.hamed: Hamed, K. H. & Rao, A. R. (1998). A modified Mann-Kendall trend test for autocorrelated data. Journal of Hydrology, 204, 182–196. DOI 10.1016/S0022-1694(97)00125-X.
cite.sen: Sen, P. K. (1968). Estimates of the regression coefficient based on Kendall's tau. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 63(324), 1379–1389. DOI 10.1080/01621459.1968.10480934.
cite.theil: Theil, H. (1950). A rank-invariant method of linear and polynomial regression analysis. Proc. KNAW, 53, 386–392. No DOI.
cite.gilbert: Gilbert, R. O. (1987). Statistical Methods for Environmental Pollution Monitoring, ch. 16. Van Nostrand Reinhold. ISBN 0-442-23050-8.
cite.bh: Benjamini, Y. & Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 57(1), 289–300. DOI 10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x.
cite.pymk: Hussain, M. M. & Mahmud, I. (2019). pyMannKendall. Journal of Open Source Software, 4(39), 1556. DOI 10.21105/joss.01556. Version 1.4.3.
cite.power: These data were obtained from the NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project funded through the NASA Earth Science/Applied Science Program.
cite.hydro: HydroSHEDS basin outline: Lehner, B. & Grill, G. (2013). Hydrological Processes, 27(15), 2171–2186. DOI 10.1002/hyp.9740.
cite.acker: Acker, J. G., McMahon, E., Shen, S., Hearty, T. & Casey, N. (2009). Time-series analysis of remotely-sensed SeaWiFS chlorophyll. EARSeL eProceedings, 8(2). NASA NTRS 20090042747.
